parents.title: Two small independent shifts turn logarithmic phases into a bilinear polynomial

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Averaging over small product shifts xy changes n^{-it} to (n+xy)^{-it} at controlled boundary cost, making xy/n uniformly small. Taylor truncation then turns log(1+xy/n) into a finite polynomial phase Σα_j x^j y^j, with degree proportional to log t/log N; that growing degree is the source-stated eventual barrier, and the usefulness of two independent variables is only anticipated here.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Explains how controlled redundancy creates a uniformly polynomializable phase and relocates difficulty from transcendental oscillation to polynomial degree.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because the averaging/Taylor mechanism and its barrier are explicit; exact exponents and coefficients remain formula-sensitive.

parents.title: Completion and Cauchy-Schwarz trade sparse variables for rational spacing

parents.title: Vinogradov mean values measure when power-sum differences become uniform

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: J_{k,r}(Z) counts collisions of two k-tuples under the first r power sums. Diagonal and ambient-volume arguments give two lower scales, and the conjecture—not the local proof—says their maximum governs the count, with near-uniform counting expected beyond its threshold. The notes distinguish a recently proved sharper range from the older theorem used here because its explicit k,r dependence remains adequate when r grows with t and N.

parents.title: Translation invariance separates nonsingular tuples from residue concentration

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Common translation preserves the power-sum system, enabling an induction at a prime p matched to the variable scale. Solutions are split according to residue diversity: in the nonsingular contribution Hölder freezes most residues and Linnik rigidity removes r variables; in the singular contribution only one half initially lacks r distinct residues, and Hölder dominates it by an all-common-residue moment, after which translation and division by p yield a smaller-range instance. The two bounds combine into the induction lemma.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Shows how diversity and concentration lead to different useful reductions, and makes the analytic domination step explicit rather than falsely claiming every singular solution is globally concentrated.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after correcting the singular-case mechanism; the long computation's constants and exponents remain formula-sensitive.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: Translation invariance, the p and Z_1 choice, J_1/J_2 split, both Hölder/orthogonality arguments, Linnik application, common-residue rescaling, and final combination occur in the span.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No claim exceeds the stated hypotheses on Z, k, r, or the tracked recursive inequality.
